meaning.fil: Sabihin ang pinakabagong nangyari o pagbabago.

examples.work: I'll update the team this afternoon.
examples.everyday: I'll update you when I arrive.

check.explanation: Update means: To give the latest information. Example: I'll update the team this afternoon.
check.hint: Think about how "update" is used in this example: I'll update the team this afternoon.

explanation.en: To give the latest information. For example: I'll update the team this afternoon.
explanation.taglish: Ginagamit ito kapag nag-uulat ng kasalukuyang estado ng isang gawain.
explanation.fil: Sabihin ang pinakabagong nangyari o pagbabago.

meaning.taglish: Sabihin ang mga natapos hanggang ngayon.
meaning.fil: Ginagamit para ipaliwanag ang nagawa na hanggang ngayon.
meaning.en: To introduce progress completed up to the present.

examples.work: So far, we've completed the first draft.
examples.everyday: So far, we've packed two bags.

dialogue.speaker: Coworker
dialogue.text: How is the draft coming along?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So far, we've completed the first draft.

dialogue.speaker: Coworker
dialogue.text: Great. What still needs to be checked?

check.explanation: Use 'finished' after 'we have' (we've): So far, we've finished the draft. 'Finish' is the base form; this pattern needs the past participle.
check.hint: Read the complete example aloud: So far, we've completed the first draft.

grammarTip.explanation: 'We've' means 'we have'. Use have + past participle for progress up to now: 'We've finished the draft.' Tandaan muna ang useful chunk na 'We've finished...'.

speaking.scenario: Your manager asks what has been completed and what remains.
hints: So far, we've ___. We still need to ___.
Use your own details or imagine a situation. Pauses are okay.
A short clear message is enough; add details only if useful.
speaking.oneMinuteGoal: Use the sentence starter to give a clear message with one useful detail. Stop when your message is complete, even before one minute.
speaking.twoMinuteGoal: Optional extension: add a reason, an example, or a next step. You do not need to fill two minutes.
speaking.modelResponse: So far, we've completed the first draft and checked the numbers. We still need to review the conclusion. I expect to send the final version tomorrow afternoon.
selfReview: I answered the situation with a clear main message.
I included the detail or question the listener needs.
I chose one sentence to improve or practice again.
preparationQuestions: What detail will make it clear?

durationGuidance.en: One and two minutes are optional practice targets, not minimums. A shorter complete message counts. Start with two or three sentences, then add detail if useful.
durationGuidance.taglish: Optional targets lang ang isa o dalawang minuto. Puwedeng mas maikli basta malinaw ang mensahe. Magsimula sa dalawa o tatlong pangungusap.
durationGuidance.fil: Gabay lamang ang isa o dalawang minuto, hindi kailangang abutin. Sapat ang mas maikling sagot kung malinaw ang mensahe.

speaking.modelResponseNote: This is one short example, not a script to memorize or a timed one-minute answer. Your details and wording may differ.

prompt.en: Before speaking, try to recall a useful expression from Day 2. Use it if it fits today's situation; no extra recording is needed.
prompt.taglish: Bago magsalita, subukang alalahanin ang isang expression sa Day 2. Gamitin kung bagay sa situation today; hindi kailangan ng dagdag na recording.
prompt.fil: Bago magsalita, alalahanin ang isang pahayag mula sa Araw 2. Gamitin kung angkop; hindi kailangan ng dagdag na rekording.
